title: What If a Martian Dust Storm Hit You? The Movie Got It Wrong

scenes.text: What if a Martian dust storm hit you? The movie got it wrong.
In The Martian, 105 mile an hour winds wreck a crew's base and strand an astronaut.
But the air on Mars is only about 1 percent as dense as Earth's.
So a 100 mile an hour gust pushes with about the force of an 11 mile an hour breeze.
The real enemy is the dust. Grains about a micron wide cling to suits, habitats and equipment.
Whole-planet storms are real: one hid Mars in 1971. You'd survive the wind. The dust is the problem.

description:
What if a Martian dust storm hit you?
Winds there can top 100 miles an hour, but the air is so thin it feels like a gentle breeze. The dust is the real danger.
